Six microphones, a 40 mm graphene driver and 50 hours of battery in a frame that weighs 254 grams. Scroll to take it apart.

01 Inside

Eight layers per cup, stacked in the order sound travels.

Cushion, driver, battery, audio chip, mics, shell, ring and swivel yoke. Every part comes apart for repair.

  • Ear cushionSlow-return foam, magnetic mount
  • 40 mm driverGraphene-coated dome
  • 1,250 mAh cellUp to 50 h, swappable
  • SS-2 audio chipRuns ANC 48,000 times a second
  • 6-mic arrayBeamformed calls and ANC sensing
  • Cup shellGlass-filled polymer
  • Outer ringMachined aluminium
  • Swivel yokeSteel pivot, folds flat
02 Driver & ANC

One driver plays your music and the opposite of the room.

Outside noise reaches the microphones first. The SS-2 chip computes the inverse wave and the driver plays it under your music, so the two cancel before they reach your ear.

Noise + anti-noise = what reaches you
03 Rebuild

Built to come apart, so it lasts.

Cushions click on with magnets. The battery comes out with one screw. When a part wears out you replace that part, not the headphones.

04 Wear

254 grams you stop noticing after the first hour.

Low clamp force and slow-return foam spread the weight across the crown instead of your ears. Put it on at boarding, take it off at arrivals.
